parsed.doc_summary: Morgan Lewis law-firm alert (Aug 21, 2026) on algorithmic rent-pricing litigation. For in-scope Jersey City, NJ, its table supports one rule: Jersey City Code § 218-12 (effective June 2025), a ban on landlord use of algorithmic rent coordination services. Hoboken ch. 158 is also listed. Other cities in the document (SF, San Diego, Berkeley, Santa Ana) are in scope but are only mentioned in the table or litigation summary.

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Landlords in Jersey City may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ordinance is enforced publicly and through private actions, with fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic rent coordination services; fines up to $2,000 per day
rules.effective_date_note: Month-level date from the law-firm alert table ("effective June 2025"); the ordinance text was not provided.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary source only. The NJ FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43) may preempt this ordinance once it takes effect, but this document does not mention that.
